title: Palestinian presidency warns Israeli attacks on Al-Aqsa risk igniting ‘religious conflict’
summary:
Palestinian presidency warns Israeli attacks on Al-Aqsa risk igniting ‘religious conflict’

The Palestinian presidency has warned that escalating Israeli attacks on Islamic holy sites risk triggering a religious conflict across the region.

In a statement carried by the Wafa news agency, the presidency said Israeli forces and settlers had intensified their assaults on Al-Aqsa Mosque and other sacred sites.

“Systematic attacks have crossed all red lines and could ignite a wider religious conflict with serious consequences for the region and the world,” it said.

The warning followed an attempt by “Colonists” to burn a mosque in Beita, northwest of Nablus, and spray racist slogans across its walls. The incident coincided with Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir’s “storming of Al-Aqsa Mosque”.

“The continuation of the repeated attacks, and the accompanying incitement, is the full responsibility of the occupying government, which is pushing matters toward this dangerous escalation.”

The presidency urged the international community to take “immediate and serious action to stop these crimes”.

title: UK urged to act 'comprehensively' against Israel's settlement plans
summary:
UK urged to act 'comprehensively' against Israel's settlement plans

Submitted by Imran Mulla on Tue, 09/01/2026 - 10:53
Labour Muslim Network and International Centre of Justice for Palestinians publish briefing in response to E1 settlement project
Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham pictured in July (AFP)
Off

The Labour Muslim Network (LMN) and International Centre of Justice for Palestinians (ICJP) have published a legal briefing urging the British government to act "urgently and comprehensively" in response to Israel's E1 settlement project.

The briefing, entitled "Priority Measures for UK Policy on Palestine", comes as Andy Burnham's government is expected to announce a raft of new measures on Israel this month.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said last month that the government would announce "measures" against Israel over the new E1 settlement project east of Jerusalem that would effectively cut the occupied West Bank in two.

The LMN, a group within the Labour Party, told Middle East Eye: "The Israeli government’s E1 settlement project could destroy the future of a viable Palestinian state.

"Settlement expansion, settler violence and terrorism, and the forcible displacement of Palestinian communities in the West Bank are accelerating on a daily basis."

The LMN added: "The UK government and the international community as a whole must act urgently and comprehensively in response to this destructive proposal before potentially irreversible damage is done."

Last month, MEE reported that Burnham's government is poised to announce a raft of new policies on Israel in September, including a ban on goods from illegal Israeli settlements.

Miliband in particular is pushing for stronger measures and has been consulting a range of civil society organisations, MEE understands.

Andy Burnham should not cave to right-wing attacks on Ali Milani
Read More »

But pro-Israel groups are campaigning for the government to weaken its policies and not implement a full ban on the import of settlement foods.

The briefing by the LMN and the ICJP, published on Tuesday, says: "The legal framework governing the settlements is firmly established in international humanitarian law, including treaties to which the UK is a party.

"The UK is required not only to respect international humanitarian law but also, under Common Article 1 of the Geneva Conventions, to ensure respect for it in all circumstances."

It adds: "The UK Government should establish a robust and tangible policy approach to Israel’s illegal settlement enterprise", including a "full ban on British citizens and businesses conducting economic and financial activities in illegal Israeli settlements as well as in activities that assist the wider illegal settlement economy".

UK should 'press for Security Council resolution'

Labour Friends of Israel (LFI), a lobby group within the Labour Party, published a report earlier this month apparently justifying some illegal Israeli settlements in occupied Palestine and urging the British government not to ban goods produced by them.

LFI is believed to count more than 70 MPs as affiliates, although it no longer keeps a public list.

Burnham is under significant pressure from Labour backbenchers to ban trade with illegal Israeli settlements. 

Polling of Labour members earlier this year showed that a staggering 87 percent support a ban on trade with Israeli settlements, with only six percent opposing it. 

The LMN and ICJP briefing further argues that the Foreign Office "should report periodically to Parliament on the status of religious sites in the [occupied Palestinian territories] and on violations, restrictions and intimidation affecting worshippers and clergy of all faiths, so that the erosion of the status quo and the persecution of Muslim and Christian Palestinians are placed on the public record and can inform sanctions and other policy decisions".

Exclusive: UK to announce raft of new policies on Israel including settlement goods ban
Read More »

It adds that "the UK should press for a Security Council resolution providing for international observers to monitor violations of religious rights and of the status quo at the holy sites of Jerusalem". 

Another key issue the Burnham government could consider movement on is arms sales. 

In September 2024, the newly elected Starmer government suspended around 30 export licences for UK-made arms after assessing there was a "clear risk" the items could be used in Gaza in serious violations of international humanitarian law.

The licensing of UK-made F-35 components exported directly to Israel was suspended. Significantly, however, parts sent to a global F-35 programme spare parts pool that could end up in Israel were exempted.

UK-made F-35 components make up 15 percent of every F-35, one of the world's most sophisticated fighter jets, which Israel used extensively in its campaign in Gaza, as well as in Lebanon and Iran. 

The briefing argues that since the UK is party to the Arms Trade Treaty, the government should "suspend all remaining arms export licences to Israel" and "suspend licences for F-35 components entering the global supply chain where UK-origin components could ultimately support Israeli military operations".

title: RSS globalised: Inside the Hindu nationalist paramilitary leader's carefully staged NYC celebration
summary:
RSS globalised: Inside the Hindu nationalist paramilitary leader's carefully staged NYC celebration

Submitted by Shraddha Joshi on Tue, 09/01/2026 - 04:36
Critics say the fascist group has covertly pushed Hindutva propaganda while masquerading as a cultural organisation using the language of spirituality
Mohan Bhagwat on the Infosys Theatre stage, in front of a projection of a video showing him delivering a speech next to the image of Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar (Shraddha Joshi/MEE)
Off

Madison Square Garden, the legendary artistic centre of New York City and a global stage for major sports and entertainment for more than 140 years, is widely regarded as the world’s most famous arena. 

On Saturday afternoon, however, the event space was home to an audience that did not quite resemble Harry Styles concert-goers or Knicks fans.

Crowds of Indian and Hindu Americans of all ages, clad in bright saffron caps, kurtas, and saris, arrived from across the country to see Mohan Bhagwat, the chief of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), a Hindu nationalist paramilitary group, whose affiliate organisations are driving violence against minorities in India. 

Hosted by American Hindus for Engagement And Dialogue (Ahead), Saturday’s "Universal Oneness Celebration" presented itself as "an afternoon of shared teaching, cultural performance, and common ground".

I attended the event as a correspondent for Middle East Eye on Saturday. What I witnessed was a careful repackaging of an entity described by critics as the "world’s largest fascist organisation" into the language of inclusion and pluralism, as escalating communal violence in India continues to claim lives daily. 

Formed in 1925, the RSS is a Hindu nationalist organisation with more than five million members across the world, with the aim of advancing the vision of Hindutva: a political project that seeks to establish India as a homogenous, Hindu ethnostate. 

One of its primary ideological progenitors, MS Golwalkar, looked towards Nazi Germany’s ethnic cleansing of European Jews as "a good lesson for us in Hindustan to learn and profit by", referring to India’s Muslims.

Likewise, VD Savarkar, regarded as the founder of the exclusionary ideology of Hindutva, viewed the Zionist project in Palestine as a model for India to embody. 

India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party was born out of the RSS’s ideological family, the Sangh Parivar and most of its leading members, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, are members of the organisation.

Senior BJP leaders, including cabinet ministers, have openly called for the killing of India's Muslims in hate speeches, referring to them as "green snakes". 

Inclusion for all, entry for some

Despite its "universal" branding, prospective attendees had to undergo identity-based vetting to attend the free event.

This meant listing an affiliated temple or organisation along with a unique five-character code for said organisation, as well as a person of reference within the group.

As part of this process, I provided information for a participating organisation that had posted its details online.

What is Hindutva and why does it matter?
Read More »

More than this, however, I believe it was my legibly Hindu, Brahmin name that allowed me to pass the vetting process without any questions, unlike others who reportedly received phone calls from organisers or eventually did not receive tickets. 

The RSS’s founding ideologues were all Hindu Brahmins, members of the dominant caste within the Hindu caste system, as were its early leaders and proponents.

To date, all but one of its chiefs have been Brahmin, and the movement has been described as born out of not only anti-Muslim sentiment, but also out of a desire to maintain Brahmanical dominance in India.

Even before entering the event, it was clear that this celebration of "inclusion" was self-selected in favour of a specific demographic, one reflective of the RSS’s values and base. 

As I joined the more than 5,000 attendees in line to enter Madison Square Garden, this became increasingly clear.

The crowd broke out into chants of "Jai Shri Ram", a Hindu religious greeting that has earned a more sinister reputation, as it is now frequently invoked by perpetrators of anti-minority violence.

Hindu nationalist groups to assemble at India Day rally in New Jersey
Read More »

The religious phrase was politicised in the 1980s as a slogan to rally Hindus for the construction of the contentious Ram Temple in the state of Uttar Pradesh's Ayodhya, which was built on the site of a 16th-century mosque demolished by Hindu mobs led by prominent BJP ministers. 

The crowds also repeatedly chanted "Vande Mataram", "I salute the motherland", referencing the national song of India.

The song has been subject to decades-long debate, as its extended version, championed by the RSS, includes references to Hindu religious deities which secular nationalists felt were at odds with the political spirit of the republic.

The later stanzas call for 70 million hands to "lift swords" and "drive out every invader who came from land and sea", a dig at the country's Muslims and Christians. 

Last month, however, the BJP-led government passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, which makes disruptions and insults to the "full" song a punishable offence. 

‘Which shakha are you part of?’

As attendees filed into MSG’s Infosys Theater, speaking to each other in Hindi, Marathi, Gujarati, and Telugu, among other languages, they made small talk about each other’s whereabouts.

A woman and her young son said that they were coming from a "shakha" near Edison, New Jersey, referring to one of the 250-plus chapters of the Hindu Swayamsevak Sangh (HSS), the RSS’s international wing.

Another attendee shared that he was a member of the Hindu Students Council, a campus-based network originated by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad of America (VHPA), a member of the Sangh family.

An event volunteer recounted his experiences in Hindu Yuva, a similar campus-based project of the Sangh.

Many attendees wore yellow wristbands from event-organised bus rides from their temples and community centres.

On its website, Ahead, whose leadership is intimately tied to the RSS and BJP according to research by anti-Hindutva group Savera, listed more than 250 partner organisations across the country, ranging from HSS Shakhas, Sangh-affiliated student organisations, and religious and cultural groups that had sent members to the event.

Outside the event, Rishi Arun, a member of the Anti Imperialist South Asian Alliance, Philadelphia (AISA Philly), and South Asian Left (Salam) - two of the organisations protesting against the gathering - told Middle East Eye that "the people that are coming to the event have gathered here as a result of a decades-long project by Hindutva to legitimise itself amongst the South Asian diaspora, specifically among religious communities in the United States".

"These organisations have covertly pushed Hindutva propaganda while masquerading as cultural organisations, and using the language of universality, spirituality, and often inclusion," he said.

A celebration of culture

The event began with a percussion exposition that journeyed through three types of South Asian drumming styles, but it was not until the Maharashtrian Dhol Tasha, which event organisers described as having military roots, that the auditorium came alive with excitement. 

Audience members clapped and whistled as an image of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj, a 17th-century Maratha king, was projected on screen.

Although many historians dispute this reading, Hindu nationalists have recast his legacy as one of the earliest examples of armed Hindu opposition against Muslim rule in India.

Following brief informational videos on "Hindu Dharma" and the nation of "Bharat", the programme featured a dance showcase in which a New Jersey-based Indian dance troupe performed to songs representing all regions of the world.

The crowd erupted in cheers as the dancers celebrated the Middle East region with Bahraini singer Flipperachi’s "Fa9la", which was the viral entry song for the Pakistani villain in Dhurandar, a 2025 Bollywood film that has been described as a Hindu nationalist "revenge fantasy".

The "Universal Oneness" event captivated its audience with a curated presentation of culture that evoked Hindutva sentiments, without having to verbalise these ties directly. 

Hindutva in interfaith harmony

Following the arts programming, the event turned to a more sober note, as religious leaders from all major faith groups took the stage, representing the "One World, One Humanity" interfaith summit.

Mohan Bhagwat stood in the centre, flanked by Jewish rabbis, Muslim imams, and clergy members of other faiths. 

Bawa Jain, founder of the World Council of Religious Leaders, introduced a "call to action" in commemoration of the "centenary of the RSS", reaffirming global commitments to interfaith harmony.

The event leadership welcomed faith leaders for brief remarks, including Muslim Imam Talib Shareef, who was praised by organisers for his 30 years of service in the US military. 

Earlier in the day, Bhagwat had addressed the interfaith summit, stating that "if any Hindu thinks there should be no Muslims in India, he will not remain Hindu".

Human rights watchdog Genocide Watch has stated that India is in the preceding phases of an anti-Muslim genocide, crediting the RSS with arming and training Hindu groups to commit organised violence.

Rewriting the RSS’s global brand

In his 40-minute culminating speech, Bhagwat told the crowd that "every nation has a destiny to fulfil" and that of "Bharat" is to "make the world realise" the idea of "unity in diversity".

Many Hindu nationalists use "Bharat" for the country, claiming it was the original name of the "motherland" before Muslim rulers called it "Hindustan" and British rulers called it "India". 

On Sunday, the RSS leadership praised the New York City event on X, calling it an initiative "taken for global outreach", as part of Mohan Bhagwat’s tour to the US, Canada and UK. 

Safa Ahmed, board member of the Indian American Muslim Council, and a co-organiser of the protest outside Saturday's event, told MEE that Bhagwat's words were "tailored for the American audience". 

"[Bhagwat's] words are one thing. And the bloodshed that the RSS commits on a near-daily basis in India is entirely another," she said.

'[Bhagwat's] words are one thing. And the bloodshed that the RSS commits on a near daily basis in India is entirely another'

- Safa Ahmed, Indian American Muslim Council

Ahmed referenced the writing of the RSS's second chief, MS Golwalkar, who wrote that minorities must be "wholly subordinated to the Hindu Nation", stating that ultimately, that was the "RSS's version of a perfect Muslim". 

Last week, the US Commission on International Religious Freedom called on the US government to sanction the RSS for its role in "violent attacks against religious minorities, including Christians, Dalits, Muslims, and Sikhs".

The committee also urged the government to revoke Bhagwat’s visa.

In India, RSS shakhas end their prayers with "Bharat Mata ki jai" or "victory to Mother India". Its global affiliates have made the phrase their own, adapting the vision of Indian and Hindu nationalism to their present-day, diaspora context.

As the "Universal Oneness" event came to an end, the crowd broke into this version of the chant: "Vishwa dharma ki jai", "Victory to universal dharma", symbolising an RSS globalised.

title: Iran president offers olive branch even as US restarts attacks
summary:
Iran president offers olive branch even as US restarts attacks

Submitted by MEE staff on Tue, 09/01/2026 - 10:31
Masoud Pezeshkian says his country would be willing to reciprocate if the US returns to the June interim deal
Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian arrives for a SCO+ format meeting of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) summit in Bishkek, 1 September 2026 (Vyacheslav Prokofyev/AFP/Sputnik)
Off

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian has offered an olive branch to US President Donald Trump even after several soldiers and civilians were killed in an US strike on Larak Island.

Speaking on Monday before travelling to Bishkek for a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit, Pezeshkian said Iran was "not looking for war” but would “never sit still in the face of any aggression”.

Iran “will give a decisive response to the aggressors” if attacked again, he said, according to the Fars news agency, but also said his country would immediately reciprocate if the US fulfilled its commitments under an interim deal signed in June, state media reported. 

"I state explicitly that if the United States returns to its commitments under the aforementioned memorandum of understanding, the Islamic Republic of Iran will immediately take reciprocal action," Pezeshkian said, according to the Iran presidency's website.

US forces bombed Larak Island on Sunday, the official state broadcaster IRIB reported.

It marked Washington’s first attack on Iran since July and raised fears of another escalation in the Israeli-US war against the country.

Following the strike, Iran urged the UN Security Council in a letter to demand that Washington end its attacks.

The letter, addressed to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres by Gholamhossein Darzi, Tehran’s deputy permanent representative and ambassador to the UN, on Monday described the attacks as a "a clear violation of the sovereignty and territorial integrity" of Iran. 

Darzi also accused the US and others involved in the attacks of war crimes and crimes against humanity in the war on Iran. 

He also stressed that while Iran had show restraint, its forces "would not hesitate" to respond to any further strikes. 

Economic strains

The impact of the war on the global economy has been highly damaging, particularly after Iran closed off the crucial Strait of Hormuz waterway.

The number of vessels sailing through the Strait of Hormuz saw little change on Monday, with preliminary ship-tracking data from Kpler showing the transit of five commodity vessels. 

Trump's vow to escalate on Iran rings hollow amid warnings from top US generals
Read More »

Four of those vessels entered the waterway and one exited.

One of the vessels that entered was an empty handy-sized gas tanker which travelled via the Iranian route. The other three were laden dry bulk carriers.

On Tuesday, Central Bank Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati said that Iran had sufficient foreign currency reserves despite the recent ramping up of US sanctions.

"I am telling the president of the United States: Iran has (foreign) currency and it has enough," he said. 

Hemmati indicated that the central bank was ready to inject up to $2bn into the foreign exchange market to calm recent volatility.

He added that the central bank was continuing to collect foreign currency receivables and had domestic reserves as well as other resources.

"I tell the people with complete honesty that economic conditions and livelihood management have become difficult, but collapse has never happened and will never happen," he stressed.

"These claims are just psychological warfare and the dust will settle soon."

title: Israeli attacks on Gaza intensify with five killed in last 24 hours, says health ministry
summary:
Israeli attacks on Gaza intensify with five killed in last 24 hours, says health ministry

Israeli attacks on Gaza have escalated, with five Palestinians killed in the last 24 hours, the Palestinian health ministry is reporting.

On Tuesday morning, at least seven air strikes hit an area west of Gaza City within a 10-minute period, killing a child, while Israeli soldiers opened fire in Deir el-Balah, killing another child.

Palestinian journalist Abdulrahman Ismail reported in a post on X that the attacks in Gaza City targeted an area "near a field hospital and thousands of tents sheltering displaced Palestinians".

"Quadcopter drones then surrounded the area, opening fire and dropping explosives at anyone moving, as the sound of clashes echoed nearby. Israeli drones simultaneously spread across Gaza City, while smoke bombs were reported over Al-Shati," Ismail said.

He added that the scenes bore "a disturbing resemblance to previous incidents involving Israeli special forces operating on the ground, but what exactly unfolded remains unclear".

Ismail said that people remain trapped in the area.

Mai Elawawda, Medical Aid for Palestine's Communications Officer in Gaza, said: “Israeli military attacks have not stopped all week. We are all constantly stressed that anywhere can be evacuated or attacked by Israeli forces at any moment.”

title: Almost half of terrorism arrests in UK since 9/11 have come after Palestine Action ban
summary:
Almost half of terrorism arrests in UK since 9/11 have come after Palestine Action ban

New data has revealed that almost half of Britian's counterterrorism arrests since 9/11 coincided with the UK government's proscription of direct action group Palestine Action.

According to Home Office data, of the 6,539 arrests for terror-related activity in the UK since the 2001 attacks on the twin towers, 3,021 were in the past year.

The surge coincides with the proscription of Palestine Action in July last year - which led to thousands of arrests of people for holding signs during silent vigils in support of the group.

The ban is subject to a continuing legal challenge, which will be heard at the UK Supreme Court in November.

In the year ending 31 March, terrorism-related arrests soared by 1,434 percent with a 3,761% increase in arrests of women and girls and a 2,306% increase in arrests of those aged 30 and over.

Raj Chada, the head of criminal defence at the law firm Hodge Jones & Allen, said: "The most common terrorist in the UK at present is a pensioner at a silent vigil holding a placard."

According to the campaign group Defend Our Juries (DOJ), more than 3,600 people have been arrested so far for alleged support of Palestine Action.

"The proscription of Palestine Action is not about protecting the British public, but about protecting the UK's relationship with Israel and protecting the arms companies who, on UK soil, manufacture and supply weapons to a genocide," A DOJ spokesperson said.

"If the government was truly aiming to proscribe violent groups targeting civilians, the IDF [Israel Defense Forces] would be first on its list."

In a statement responding to the data, Ruth Ehrlich, the director of external relations at the civil rights group Liberty, said: “The staggering increase in arrests over the past year is the clearest indicator that the UK’s counter-terror laws are not fit for purpose." She added that when without public trust "counter-terror laws simply won’t work".

title: Israel warned Turkey against moving south in Syria. It did so anyway
summary:
Israel warned Turkey against moving south in Syria. It did so anyway

Submitted by Ragip Soylu on Tue, 09/01/2026 - 10:21
Turkish troops deployed to Deir ez-Zor and built a temporary bridge across the Euphrates, drawing no military response from Israel
A large Syrian flag flutters above Tishreen Park in Damascus on 4 June 2025 (Louai Beshara/AFP)
Off

Two weeks after Israel bombed a Syrian base in the north to draw a red line against Turkish troops moving south, Ankara did exactly that, with no military response from Israel.

Over the weekend, the Turkish army moved into Deir ez-Zor to establish a temporary bridge for civilians crossing the Euphrates River. Turkish soldiers, working alongside their Syrian counterparts, quickly erected the floating bridge, raised Turkish and Syrian flags, and tested the platform by driving Turkish armoured vehicles across it.

Turkish drones were hovering overhead to provide an additional layer of security for the troops, according to sources speaking to Middle East Eye.

“We will not tolerate Turkish military entrenchment moving southward because it threatens us,” Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said last month after ordering strikes on the Abu al-Duhur military airbase in northern Syria, approximately 70km from the Turkish border.

Israeli officials claimed that Turkey was preparing to move into the base, an assertion denied by Turkish and Syrian officials, as well as US envoy Tom Barrack.

Netanyahu’s spokesperson said: “Israel wouldn’t allow Turkey to entrench itself in Syria and to move steadily south toward Israel’s border.”

Turkish officials view the lack of an Israeli response to the Turkish army’s movement deep into southern Syria, nearly 180km from the Turkish border, as evidence that Netanyahu had sought to inflame tensions to score political points ahead of Israel’s critical general election in October.

🔴|Türk Silahlı Kuvvetleri (#TSK) ile #Suriye Silahlı Kuvvetleri tarafından #DeirEzZor’un El-Mayadin bölgesine yüzer seyyar köprü kuruluyor. pic.twitter.com/JDFW1RFfs7

— Külliyat (@kulliyatX) August 30, 2026

Translation: A floating pontoon bridge is being constructed in the El-Mayadin region of #DeirEzZor by the Turkish Armed Forces (#TSK) and #Syrian Armed Forces.

Carmit Valensi, a senior researcher at the Israel-based Institute for National Security Studies (INSS), believes Israel is now under greater pressure to exercise restraint towards Turkey.

“Washington has been very clear that it wants to prevent an Israeli-Turkish escalation in Syria and is actively working on a deconfliction mechanism among Israel, Turkey and Syria,” she told MEE.

“That probably creates an additional incentive for Israel to distinguish between developments that it considers genuinely threatening and Turkish activity that it can tolerate.”

Valensi said that if Israeli statements about Turkish forces moving towards the Israeli border are taken literally, there is indeed a contradiction.

“This case suggests that ‘moving south’ is not, by itself, the real red line. In practice, Israel seems more concerned with permanent Turkish military capabilities that could limit its freedom of action,” she said. “So the public rhetoric may have been broader than the actual operational threshold.”

Israel's red line

Despite Israel’s red-line rhetoric, Valensi said the country is more interested in preventing the deployment of Turkish air-defence systems, radar, and command-and-control capabilities, as well as the transfer of advanced weapons into Syria.

“In fact, the Deir ez-Zor case may actually demonstrate that Israel’s red line is less about how far south Turkey goes and more about what Turkey brings with it; engineers and bridges are one thing; air-defence systems, permanent bases and strategic capabilities are another.”

Some Israeli reports suggested that Israel was deeply concerned about the possible deployment of air-defence systems at the Abu al-Duhur military airbase. Such systems could allow Ankara to track Israeli Air Force movements over Syria during military operations targeting Iran.

'The Turkish navy enjoys an inherent advantage in the eastern Mediterranean'

- INSS report

However, a new INSS report on the issue makes clear that such a deployment would not substantially affect Israel’s “freedom of action” in Syrian airspace.

“From an operational standpoint, there is little practical difference between the deployment of Turkish radar, electronic warfare or air-defence systems in northern Syria and their deployment in southern Turkey or northern Cyprus,” the INSS report said.

“Their coverage ranges are similar, and the presence of such systems in northern Syria therefore does not in itself constitute a red line warranting the use of Israeli force.

“The same applies to the maritime domain: The Turkish navy enjoys an inherent advantage in the eastern Mediterranean, and a limited presence along the Syrian coast would not fundamentally alter the balance of power.”

title: Gaza 'ceasefire' has merely slowed the pace of societal destruction
summary:
Gaza 'ceasefire' has merely slowed the pace of societal destruction

Submitted by Ghada Majadli on Thu, 08/27/2026 - 15:31
The Israeli bombs have slowed, but many Palestinians with life-changing injuries are struggling to survive in a ravaged landscape 
A Palestinian amputee walks near destroyed buildings in Beit Hanoun, in the northern Gaza Strip, on 12 February 2025 (Omar al-Qattaa/AFP)
On

Every fourth Palestinian injured in Gaza since October 2023 lives with spinal cord or brain injuries, among other potentially life-changing conditions, the World Health Organization (WHO) recently estimated. Despite this, the entry of rehabilitation supplies remains restricted. 

Of the more than 172,000 people wounded in Gaza, 43,000 - around two percent of Gaza’s prewar population, including approximately 10,000 children - are estimated to have sustained life-changing injuries, such as limb trauma, amputations, spinal cord damage, major burns and traumatic brain injuries. More than aid agencies report that no rehabilitation equipment entered Gaza between May 2024 and 14 April 2026, while shipments containing assistive products faced an average waiting time of 136 days. 

Gaza is increasingly home to a mass population of survivors whose bodies have been permanently altered by Israeli violence, while the infrastructure necessary for them to recover and live with dignity has simultaneously been destroyed.

Even after the so-called ceasefire took effect in October, Israel has continued to deny them critical aid.

Since then, little has fundamentally changed. Palestinians continue to be killed while sleeping, shopping, or spending time at the beach. Aid deliveries and medical supplies continue to be blocked or severely restricted.

As of August, Kerem Shalom remained the only operational crossing for cargo into Gaza, while the volume of supplies entering remained insufficient to meet needs. Of 878 commercial truckloads entering Gaza between 3 and 9 August, only two reportedly carried medical equipment.

The form and pace of the violence have changed, but the conditions producing premature and preventable Palestinian death remain

Tents sheltering displaced people and some of the last standing buildings continue to be bombed daily. In less than a year since the ceasefire was announced, more than 1,300 Palestinians have been killed. 

Most Palestinians remain internally displaced. Around 82 percent of all structures in the Gaza Strip, roughly 200,000 buildings, have been damaged or destroyed, while Israeli attacks continue, and reconstruction remains far from reach. More than 1.2 million Palestinians in Gaza, around 60 percent of the population, have lost their homes. 

For the tens of thousands of people living with life-changing injuries, these conditions are particularly devastating.

Systematic destruction

Major limb injuries account for the largest share, with more than 22,000 recorded, followed by more than 5,000 limb amputations. Yet of the 2,300 amputees evaluated between September 2024 and May 2026, only 500 - less than a quarter - had been fitted with permanent prosthetics, amid severe shortages in Gaza.

One in five amputees is a child, but no rehabilitation facility in Gaza is fully functional; all are operating under severe constraints in staffing, equipment or supplies. 

This means that surviving the initial injury - whether inflicted by bombardment, gunfire or a quadcopter - does not guarantee staying alive, when the conditions necessary for treatment and recovery have themselves been systematically destroyed or denied. 

What follows is life with injury and disability amid displacement, destroyed homes, inaccessible streets and buildings, shortages of assistive devices, and a healthcare system that Israel has systematically debilitated. 

People with amputations, spinal cord injuries and traumatic brain injuries are forced to recover in tents, damaged buildings and overcrowded shelters

The question, then, is no longer only who survives Israeli bombardment, but under what conditions survivors must now live. What kind of society is being produced through mass injury, disability, and the denial of recovery?

When we speak of the hundreds of thousands of Palestinians injured in Gaza, and the unprecedented scale of life-changing injuries among them, we must also account for the mass destruction and continued denial of the material conditions that could have treated these injuries, prevented their deterioration, and alleviated some of their long-term consequences.

The scale of injury in Gaza is therefore also a story of what has been systematically denied to the survivors: treatment, rehabilitation, adequate shelter, and the conditions necessary for recovery and life with dignity.

Israel’s practice of maiming Palestinian bodies, while simultaneously attacking the infrastructure necessary to rehabilitate and sustain them, did not begin with the current genocide. During the 2018 Great March of Return, Israeli soldiers systematically shot protesters in the limbs, injuring thousands. At least 1,200 required specialised limb reconstruction treatment, according to the WHO.

Since October 2023, this logic has expanded to an unprecedented scale: hundreds of thousands of tonnes of explosives have produced mass traumatic injuries, while hospitals, rehabilitation facilities and medical workers have been attacked, and the entry of medicines and medical equipment severely restricted or blocked. 

A particularly destructive dimension of Israel’s violence lies in this simultaneity. A serious injury does not necessarily have to become a permanent disability or debilitating condition. 

What happens afterwards - whether surgery is available, infection can be prevented, physiotherapy and prosthetics can be accessed, or people have adequate nutrition, shelter and a safe environment for recovery - shapes the trajectory of that injury. In Gaza, these conditions have systematically been dismantled or denied.

Interconnected violence

This is why the maiming of Palestinian bodies and the destruction of healthcare infrastructure must be understood as interconnected forms of Israeli violence. They operate together, with the destruction of healthcare deepening and prolonging the effects of bodily injury. 

When thousands of Palestinians are left with amputations, spinal injuries, major burns, traumatic brain injuries and other long-term conditions, while the facilities necessary for their recovery are incapacitated, injury is extended across time.

Mass injury also has consequences beyond individual bodies. When tens of thousands of people require long-term care while families themselves are displaced, impoverished and struggling to secure food and shelter, the effects extend across households and communities.

People who might otherwise work, care for others, organise, rebuild or sustain communal life are instead forced to devote enormous resources simply to surviving.

Yet this devastating reality - of bombardment, killing, injury and severe restriction of aid - is increasingly being accepted as compatible with “postwar” Gaza. The declaration of a “ceasefire” in October 2025 produced a widespread sense that the war has ended, thus reducing the political urgency, media coverage and international attention that accompanied the preceding two years.

The scale of bombardment and killing has indeed decreased compared with the period before the ceasefire. But a reduction in the intensity of violence is not the same as its end. 

The world is normalising this situation: the declaration of a ceasefire as bombardment, killing, displacement and deprivation continue, albeit at a reduced scale. This follows a decades-long pattern in which Gaza has been subjected to repeated Israeli assaults, followed by ceasefire declarations that have failed to end the violence. 

Since the October 2025 ceasefire alone, more than 1,900 Palestinians have been injured, according to UN data - and the conditions that transform injury into permanent disability remain largely intact. People with amputations, spinal cord injuries and traumatic brain injuries are forced to recover in tents, damaged buildings and overcrowded shelters, often without the long-term care they require. 

A ceasefire cannot be measured only by whether the daily number of Palestinians killed has fallen. It must also be measured by whether the conditions that produce and prolong Palestinian suffering have ended. 

Yet Israel continues to occupy roughly half of the Gaza Strip behind the so-called Yellow Line, while most Palestinians remain displaced and confined to an increasingly uninhabitable and devastated territory.

Restrictions on medicines, medical equipment, rehabilitation supplies and other essential goods continue, while the healthcare, water, sanitation and housing infrastructures necessary to sustain life remain severely destroyed.

These conditions amount to a slower form of destruction. For many Palestinians, death may no longer come immediately through bombardment, but rather through an untreated injury, the absence of medication or rehabilitation, contaminated water, deteriorating public health conditions, malnutrition, or diseases that a functioning healthcare system could have treated. 

The form and pace of the violence have changed, but the conditions producing premature and preventable Palestinian death remain in place.
